answer_1.quote: We tackle the problem of after-visit care instruction generation from a medical dialog between patient and medical professional.

answer_2.quote: We use BERTScore to estimate the similarity between reference and candidate, GPT-2 perplexity for to assess the coherence (fluency) of the candidate, and concept overlap to measure the percentage of medical concepts used in both candidate in reference.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation with medical experts. We randomly sample 100 dialogues from the test set and generate candidates with each model setup setting α = 1.0. We ask five doctors to evaluate the relevance to the dialogue, medical usability (if the generated instruction can be used in any care plan), and grammatical correctness (fluency) on a scale from 1 to 5.
answer_4.guideline: We ask five doctors to evaluate the relevance to the dialogue, medical usability (if the generated instruction can be used in any care plan), and grammatical correctness (fluency) on a scale from 1 to 5. Additionally, we ask assessors to indicate degenerate generations, i.e., premature or repetitive sequences.
